answer: An agent market pays conservators to rescue a relic from a ledge before the tide rises. Each bidder proves possession of a credential issued after an in-person workshop audit; a zero-knowledge proof reveals only an epoch-specific nullifier. The market rejects a second bid with that nullifier, even from another agent account, while hiding the operator's name. A Sybil attacker needs extra audited workshops or forged credentials, not just more logins. A corrupt issuer could mint duplicates and newcomers may be excluded, so issuers face public audits and applicants need an appeal path.
